name: Train runs 5+ min over scheduled run time
definition: A train run counts when its run time over the compared stops is more than 5 minutes (over 300 s) above the scheduled run time. Only matched runs count: the trip id is a trip in the GTFS schedule published for the date. Runs LAMP records under other ids (mostly ADDED- trips) are counted separately and left out. Line-days with a planned service change are left out of the headline figure and its typical range.
used_here: late_trip_share, late_trips, trips_compared (run times, not rider trips; no rider weighting); unmatched_trips_compared, added_trips_compared

name: Excess trip time
definition: The MBTA's excess trip time is actual wait plus travel time minus a baseline wait plus travel time, per rider. Here the baseline is the published schedule, not the MBTA's fastest-month baseline, and runs are not rider-weighted.
used_here: train delay (run time minus scheduled run time), average excess per trip
source_name: MBTA OPMI Data Blog: Introducing Excess Trip Time

name: NYC subway comparison
definition: NYC Transit publishes subway reliability as time riders spend beyond the schedule (extra time waiting on the platform and extra time on the train). The same split, wait and ride, is used for rider time lost here.
used_here: rider time lost (excess wait + excess ride)

name: Expected wait
definition: For riders arriving at random times, expected wait = sum(h^2) / (2 * sum(h)) over the gaps h between trains. This is the per-rider form of the OPMI example (each rider waits half the gap they arrive in, so long gaps catch more riders): gaps of 5 and 15 minutes give 6.25 minutes, against 5 for even 10-minute gaps.
used_here: excess wait in rider time lost (actual gaps minus scheduled gaps)
source_name: MBTA OPMI Data Blog: Introducing Excess Trip Time

name: Headway (LAMP)
definition: The gap between a train leaving a stop and the previous train leaving the same stop, from the MBTA's LAMP subway performance files (headway_trunk_seconds; scheduled_headway_trunk for the schedule). Trunk gaps count every train on the shared track, so the Green Line trunk counts all branches.
used_here: long gaps, bunched, gapped, expected wait

name: Bunched and gapped (SFMTA rules)
definition: A departure is bunched when it comes less than 2 minutes after the previous train, and gapped when the gap is more than the scheduled gap plus 5 minutes. These are the SFMTA rules as described by Swiftly.
source_name: Swiftly: How Well Is America Sticking to its Promised Headways?

name: Daily completeness
definition: Scheduled trips with at least one compared run under their own trip id, divided by trips in the GTFS schedule published for that date. Counted from the schedule side, so it is never above 1. Runs under trip ids that are not scheduled that date are counted on their own (unmatched_runs_compared, added_runs_compared). A line-day is flagged low below 0.8. On days with a planned service change a low share usually reflects the diversion timetable (is_planned_change), not missing data.

name: Typical range
definition: The typical value is the median of the same measure on the 28 most recent earlier service dates of the same day type without a planned service change; the typical range is the 25th to 75th percentile (p25 to p75) of those days. Days with a planned change keep their own figures and label but do not count toward any typical value.
used_here: typical_median, typical_p25, typical_p75 on tiles and line_day_metrics

name: MBTA excess trip time and this measure
definition: Since December 2024 the MBTA reports Red, Orange and Blue Line reliability as the share of rider trips with excess trip time of 5 minutes or less: actual wait plus travel time minus a baseline from the fastest monthly median since April 2021, per rider. This board counts train runs more than 5 minutes over the scheduled run time, per train, against the timetable, with no rider weighting. The two share the 5-minute threshold only and are not comparable. The Green Line and Mattapan do not have MBTA excess trip time results yet.
used_here: late_trip_share; mbta_reference on the late tile; reference_values
source_name: MBTA Service Reliability; MBTA OPMI Data Blog: Introducing Excess Trip Time

name: Planned service changes
definition: A line-day has a planned service change when the GTFS timetable published for it runs under a diversion service (service_id starting DIV) or an MBTA alert announced at least 24 hours ahead replaces part of the line with shuttle buses or suspends it between at least two of its stations (LAMP archive of the MBTA service alerts feed). Station closures, elevator work, single tracking without a diversion timetable, notices and alerts for other routes are listed but do not set the flag. These line-days are left out of the headline tiles, the line totals, the worst-line test and every typical range, and stay in the day views with a label. The MBTA leaves planned diversion days out of its Service Delivery Policy results.
used_here: service_changes.parquet; is_planned_change, planned_change_label on line_daily, line_day_metrics and line_day_completeness
source_name: Fall 2024 Service Delivery Policy Report; LAMP_RT_ALERTS

name: Matched trips and duplicate stop events
definition: LAMP sometimes records the same train at the same station twice under two trip ids (one of them an ADDED- id). When one train set is recorded at the same station in the same direction within 60 seconds under two trip ids, one stop event is kept: the matched trip first, then a trip that is not ADDED-, then the trip with more stop events. The other is dropped and counted (duplicate_stop_events_dropped).

name: Rider-weighted headway adherence
definition: Estimated share of riders whose wait was no longer than the allowed wait, after the MBTA passenger wait time standard: the scheduled headway, and on the Green Line trunk (stations on two or more branches) 3 minutes or the scheduled headway, whichever is larger. For each gap h between trains at a station, riders arriving at random wait no longer than the allowance T for the share min(h, T) / h; the gap carries riders in proportion to h times the arrival rate. Arrival rate = average daily fare-gate entries for the station, line, day type and period / period length, split 50/50 between directions. Stations without gates (Green Line surface stops, most of Mattapan) all get the average rate of the gated stations on the line. Holidays use Sunday entries. Transfers inside stations are not counted. Gate entries come from the MBTA Open Data Portal and run through August 31, 2026; the station, line, day type and period averages from those dates are used for later service dates (basis dates on each row of the rider weights). Planned-change line-days are left out.
used_here: rider_headway_adherence.parquet (rider_weighted_share, unweighted_share, departure_share) by line, day type and period
source_name: MBTA Service Delivery Policy (Fall 2024), passenger wait time standard

name: MBTA reliability target and 2024 result
definition: Reference values from the MBTA: the Service Delivery Policy target for rapid transit reliability is 90%; the 2024 weekday rapid transit result was 82.8% (excess trip time, Red, Orange and Blue Lines). They are a different measure from this board's and are shown as labelled references only.
used_here: reference_values in board_data.json; mbta_reference on the late tile
source_name: Fall 2024 Service Delivery Policy Report (Figure 15, Table A10)
